This article collects the models, export configuration, workbook templates and SQL files used in the guides.

Use [Getting started](form.tools.html) for workbook operations and [Load tables from SQL](sql-loading.html) for loading.

## Get the resources

```{r resources-archive, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Read the package version used in the downloadable archive name.
resources_version <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("form.tools"))
# Offer the archive on the website and installed resources in the package guide.
if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
  # Link the ZIP archive containing all the examples below.
  cat(sprintf("[Download all examples (%s, ZIP)](../form.tools-resources-%s.zip).\n",
    resources_version, resources_version))
} else {
  # Identify the packages supplying the offline resources.
  cat("The example files are installed with `form.tools` and its dependency `form.model`.\n")
}
```

The archive name includes the `form.tools` version. Its `examples/survey/` directory preserves the query paths.

```{r resources-directories}
# Locate the source model and SQL queries installed with this package.
resources_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", package = "form.tools")
# Locate the shared workbook model and templates installed with form.model.
workbook_resources_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", package = "form.model")
```

## Example downloads

```{r resources-downloads, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Describe the packaged SQL files and the shared workbook resources.
resources <- data.frame(
  File = c("form-source.yaml", "export.yaml", "queries/surveys.sql", "queries/observations.sql", "README.md",
    "form.yaml", "form.xlsx", "form-empty.xlsx"),
  Package = c(rep("form.tools", 5L), rep("form.model", 3L)),
  Purpose = c("Source table model for SQL loading.", "Row and field rules for an export preview.",
    "Select the requested survey.",
    "Select its related observations.", "Directory layout and usage notes.",
    "Workbook model for writing and splitting.", "Populated workbook to split.",
    "Empty template for output workbooks."))
# Display file names without depending on a network connection.
resource_labels <- sprintf("`%s`", resources$File)
# Add download links only when building the website.
if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
  # Resolve downloads relative to this article.
  resource_targets <- paste0("../examples/survey/", resources$File)
  # Keep the Markdown download as its original file rather than an HTML page.
  resource_targets[resources$File == "README.md"] <-
    "https://ultreia-io.github.io/form.tools/examples/survey/README.md"
  # Render one link for each resource.
  resource_labels <- sprintf("[`%s`](%s)", resources$File, resource_targets)
}
# Replace file names with the labels for this output format.
resources$File <- resource_labels
# Render the complete list as a Markdown table.
cat(knitr::kable(resources, format = "pipe"), sep = "\n")
```

The source and workbook models illustrate separate operations. They do not define a source-to-workbook conversion.

## Form model schema

`form.tools` uses the versioned form model contract supplied by `form.model`.

Both example YAML files declare `schema_version: "1.0.0"` and are read with `form.model::read_form_model()`.

See [form.model][form-model-schema] for the form model schema.

[form-model-schema]: https://ultreia-io.github.io/form.model/articles/form.model.html

## Export configuration schema

`read_form_export()` checks the survey's `export.yaml` against the schema selected by its `schema_version`.

`export_schema()` exposes that contract. `prepare_form_export()` checks the plan against the models and callbacks.

## SQL query contract

- Supply one `<sheet>.sql` file per model sheet; a sheet named `schema.table` uses `schema.table.sql`.
- Return exactly the modeled columns in their declared order, including headers for empty results.
- Apply the supplied parameter list in every query using the selected backend's parameter syntax.
- Declare ordering with `ORDER BY` when row order matters.

The SQLite queries use `?` placeholders for a bound survey identifier.

Queries are trusted input supplied by the consumer. Database credentials and connection objects are not package resources.

```{r resources-source-model, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Display the source model directly from the installed example.
cat("```yaml\n", paste(readLines(file.path(resources_directory, "form-source.yaml")),
  collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```
